Canaan Sells 3,952 ETH and 54 BTC for $13.9M, Uses $5.4M for Share Buyback Canaan said it sold all 3,952 ETH and 54 BTC held for sale at the end of August, at average prices of about $2,400 per ETH and $79,000 per BTC, generating approximately $13.9 million in cash. Of the proceeds, about $5.4 million was used to repurchase 13.6 million ADSs. The company still held 1,868 BTC at the end of August and said it plans to maintain a strategic digital asset reserve. — link

18 State AGs Push Back on CLARITY Act Ahead of Key Senate Vote New York Attorney General Letitia James led a bipartisan coalition of 17 other state attorneys general urging Congress to oppose the current version of the CLARITY Act ahead of Tuesday’s key procedural vote. The coalition argues that the bill could weaken state-level authority to pursue crypto fraud and investor-protection cases, while expanding the SEC’s ability to preempt state registration regimes. The group is calling on Congress to preserve states’ existing enforcement and registration powers over digital assets. — link

Bitdeer AI Secures 65.1MW AI Cloud Capacity in Malaysia, Says Active Project Pipeline Exceeds $7 Billion in Potential Contract Value Bitdeer AI secured 65.1 MW of AI Cloud data center capacity at the A202 facility at its existing Johor campus in Malaysia under a 10-year data center services agreement, with energization expected in Q3 2027. The addition brings its secured AI Cloud data center capacity to approximately 206.5 MW, or about 59% of its 350 MW target by Q1 2028. The company said its active AI Cloud project pipeline now represents more than $7 billion in potential contract value. — link

U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.012%, Highest Intraday Level Since 2007, as Oil Surge Fuels Inflation Fears WSJ data showed the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.012% on Monday, its highest intraday level since 2007, as rising oil prices intensified inflation concerns and fueled a selloff in Treasurys. Brent crude briefly approached $110 a barrel amid heightened Middle East tensions. The Nasdaq fell about 1% in early trading as AI safety concerns weighed on technology stocks, while investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s rate decision on Wednesday. — link
